data.title: Kier Group Advances Share Buyback, Boosting Treasury Holdings
data.description:
An announcement from Kier Group plc ( (GB:KIE) ) is now available.

Kier Group plc has continued its previously announced share buyback programme, repurchasing 250,000 ordinary shares between 7 and 11 September 2026 through Deutsche Numis at volume‑weighted average prices ranging from about 242p to 253p per share. The company intends to hold these repurchased shares in treasury rather than cancel them.

Following these latest purchases, Kier has bought a total of 6,648,654 shares under the buyback and will have 452,875,390 ordinary shares in issue, of which 17,627,122 are held in treasury, leaving 435,248,268 voting shares outstanding. The transaction, made in line with U.K. listing and market abuse regulations, slightly reduces free‑float and may support earnings per share, while clarifying the denominator for shareholders’ disclosure and transparency obligations.

data.title: Tribal Group Agrees £189m Sale to Main Capital and Plans AIM Delisting
data.description:
Tribal Group plc ( (GB:TRB) ) has issued an update.

Tribal Group plc has agreed to sell all of its operating subsidiaries, including its Student Information Solutions division and Etio, to Thames Bidco Limited, a vehicle controlled by private equity investor Main Capital Partners, for approximately £189.3 million in cash. The deal, which constitutes a fundamental change of business under AIM rules and a restricted action under the Takeover Code, is subject to shareholder approval and satisfaction of a national security condition.

If the transaction completes, the board intends to delist Tribal’s shares from AIM and place the company into a members’ voluntary liquidation, distributing net sale proceeds to investors after covering PLC and liquidation costs from existing group cash resources. The board rejected an unsolicited, highly conditional alternative proposal from SilverTree Equity Partners, arguing Main Capital’s offer provides superior certainty and deliverability, while positioning Tribal to accelerate product innovation, cloud adoption and international expansion in a sector benefiting from strong structural growth trends.

data.description:

Avrasya Gayrimenkul Yatirim Ortakligi A.S. has disclosed a detailed six-month 2026 consolidated participation finance principles information form, confirming that its core activities and its articles of association do not include prohibited sectors such as alcohol, pork, gambling or tobacco. The company also reports no non-compliant share privileges or court or regulatory findings related to support for activities that contravene participation finance standards.

Despite this, the disclosure identifies limited non-compliant elements in its operations, notably some financial sector activities and certain tourism and entertainment-related income, resulting in 0.52% of total income, 4.23% of assets and 13.5% of liabilities classified as not complying with participation finance principles. The bulk of its TL 603.9 million total income is deemed compliant, driven by other operating income, fair value increases and subsidiary sale profits, suggesting that while the company maintains substantial alignment with participation finance norms, stakeholders should note the modest exposure in assets and payables that fall outside these guidelines.

data.description:

The filing reflects Manulife’s ongoing use of U.S. and Canadian trustees to structure subordinated debt offerings that qualify under Canadian capital rules, underscoring the company’s active management of Tier 2 capital and long-term funding.
